Site / country: University of Minnesota West Central Research and Outreach Center dairy farm, Morris, Minnesota, USA
Species / cultivar: Dairy cattle (crosses of Holstein, Montbeliarde, Viking Red, Jersey and Normande)
Area definition: Each treatment paddock; not the PV footprint or total project area
Comparator: No access to shade from PV, trees or buildings
Implementation evidence: A 30-kW ground-mounted PV system was installed in a pasture in summer 2018 (PDF p. 2).
Production outcome: Milk production: 13.9 (SEM 1.5) kg for shade vs 15.5 (SEM 1.5) kg for no shade, Table 3; not significantly different (P > 0.10). Daily milk production measurement described in Methods.
Microclimate / water / welfare: Afternoon respiration: 66.4 vs 78.3 breaths/min (P < 0.05); daytime body temperature between milkings: 38.9 vs 39.1 deg C (P < 0.05). Shade cows had dirtier bellies and lower legs.
Missing data / source issues: PV footprint, row spacing, ground coverage ratio, module model, annual electricity yield and LER not reported. Coordinates in the paper identify the weather station and are not assigned to the PV array. Capacity reported as kW, without explicit AC/DC designation.
Study limitations: Cows used the study pasture only during four rotational grazing periods. No significant milk-yield benefit was demonstrated; heat stress was mild.
Source pages: PDF pp. 2-3 (system and design), p. 6 Table 2, p. 7 Table 3, p. 11 Table 6

Site / country: Gold Tree Solar Farm, California Polytechnic State University, San Luis Obispo County, California, USA
Study period: Pilot: third week of November 2020, four days; main: January 2021, 16 days. Table 1 Jan 3-18 conflicts with weather discussion citing Jan 22-23 during last study days.
Capacity status / basis: Converted from reported 4.5 MW; main text does not specify AC/DC
Orientation / tracking: Single-axis sun-tracking; cardinal axis orientation not reported
Area definition: Total solar farm on sheep pasture, converted from 7.5 ha
Comparator: Native rangeland without solar panels, using corresponding 1-day or 4-day grazing rotation
Implementation evidence: Operating 4.5-MW ground-mounted single-axis tracking solar facility on 7.5 ha sheep pasture; field grazing experiment (PDF pp. 3-4).
Production outcome: Body-weight gain not measured because pregnancy would confound change. Forage quantity was lower at solar site, but g/ha units in p. 7 are questionable and not normalized into biomass-yield fields.
Microclimate / water / welfare: Logger-estimated grazing time: solar 4d 45.65±0.35% versus native 4d 44.02±0.47%; solar 1d 43.30±0.46% versus native 1d 39.95±0.39% of total time (mean±SEM). Treatment x management P<0.01. Manual observations showed an opposite grazing pattern and were not statistically tested.
Missing data / source issues: Module manufacturer/model/count, installation year, panel height/tilt/spacing, annual energy yield, LER and measured animal growth not reported. Site coordinates not reported. Date discrepancy retained. Published forage relative percentage wording is internally inconsistent with displayed means; not adopted.
Study limitations: System comparison with different prior grazing histories; solar groups alone received ~23 kg alfalfa hay/group on days 2-4, supplying ~50% dry-matter intake. Logger grazing includes hay consumption; January senescent forage during drought. Short exploratory study, not causal isolation of PV shading.
Source pages: PDF p. 3 system; p. 4 design and Table 1; p. 7 results; p. 8 contrary manual observations and supplementation; p. 10 coverage and p. 11 no weight-gain measurement

Site / country: Animal Biometeorology Laboratory, São Paulo State University, Jaboticabal, Brazil
Species / cultivar: Ovis aries; nine adult nonpregnant, nonlactating Corriedale ewes
Study period: 20 consecutive days between August and September 2019, 08:00-17:00; electricity January-December 2019
Capacity status / basis: Calculated: 10 x 335 Wp / 1000; inverter separately reported as Fronius 3 kWp
PV manufacturer / model: Canadian Solar / CS6Ue335P as extracted from source; verify model typography against PDF
Area definition: PV roof 4 x 5 m; paddock 1900 m²; reported shaded area 19.3 m² (2.14 m²/ewe)
Comparator: Periods spent in sun versus voluntarily in PV shade
Implementation evidence: Ten operating PV panels shading an experimental paddock; 2019 electricity monitored and sheep measured (PDF pp. 2-3).
Production outcome: Milk yield, meat production and weight gain not evaluated.
Microclimate / water / welfare: Midday shade radiant heat load ~500 versus ~700 W/m² in sun, reported ~30% reduction. With increasing time in shade under high irradiance, wool-surface temperature decreased 7-8°C and skin temperature 1.0-1.5°C. Vaginal temperature remained 38.5-39.2°C; authors caution against causal interpretation of small (~0.2°C) shade-associated differences.
Missing data / source issues: Azimuth, installation date, total project boundary, row spacing, LER and livestock yield not reported. Abstract mean body mass 70±12 kg conflicts with Methods 78 kg (SD12); fleece variation also differs. Do not silently reconcile.
Study limitations: Nine animals, 20-day observation; shade thermal assessment performed after animal measurements for ten days. Carbon avoidance calculated using emission factors, not directly measured animal methane. Core-temperature rhythm and wool insulation confound interpretation.
Source pages: PDF p. 2 system/design; p. 3 electricity method and physiological results; p. 4 interpretation; pp. 5-6 electricity/production limitations

Site / country: University of Queensland Gatton Solar Research Facility, Australia
Species / cultivar: Sheep in tracker fields; Gatton panic, African star grass, Sabi grass
Study period: Pasture samples January/March 2021; dual-axis field grazing started 2016
Capacity status / basis: Reported whole-facility output 3.275 MW; section ratings use capped/degraded bases and must not be summed blindly.
Orientation / tracking: Fixed tilt, single-axis and dual-axis sections
Area definition: Approximately 10 ha whole facility; fixed/single/dual sections 6/2/2 ha
Implementation evidence: Methods explicitly confirm sheep grazing in single- and dual-axis tracker fields, with grazing infrastructure; fixed-array older/pregnant sheep unsuitable (pp.2-3).
Production outcome: Sheep actually graze single- and dual-axis tracker fields. Fixed-array measured biomass 6073 kg/ha versus model 6292 kg/ha (abstract). Long-term ungrazed model means: fixed 7798, single-axis 7671, dual-axis 7186, full sun 6766 kg/ha.
Missing data / source issues: Animal output, financial data and PV specifications not reported unless explicitly stated here. Brief review; auxiliary tables not exhaustively transcribed.
Study limitations: 25-year results are simulations, not observations. Samples selected from high-yielding ungrazed areas. Fixed arrays unsuitable for older/pregnant sheep; do not treat all configurations as confirmed grazing. Capacity and panel inventory use different capped/degraded bases.

Site / country: Outskirts of Moravsky Krumlov, South Moravia, Czech Republic; 49°03'12.1 N, 16°17'41.2 E; 340 m
Species / cultivar: Sheep, breed NR; pasture sown with 70% Lolium perenne, 25% Festuca rubra, 5% Dactylis glomerata
Study period: July, August and September of 2013, 2014 and 2015; pasture sown spring 2010
Capacity status / basis: Calculated site total: rotating 432 kWp plus stationary 650 kWp; component capacities reported pp.2-3.
Height (m; source value): Stationary lower edge ~0.65 m; rotating lower edge 0.7-3 m
Height definition: Stationary upper edge 2.2-2.5 m; rotating upper edge 2-7 m. Heights change with rotation; not a common site clearance.
Orientation / tracking: Stationary orientation NR; rotating automated swivel stands with polar-axis sun tracking and ridge radiation concentrators
Area definition: Entire solar park 8.2 ha, converted to m2; not exact grazed area or allocation to PV sections.
Comparator: Grazing versus fenced annual mowing; stationary versus rotating PV; under versus between panels. No separate off-site unshaded sheep control.
Implementation evidence: Sheep move freely around operating solar park. Mown experimental plots fenced to exclude sheep; annual mowing at end of growing period. Eight treatments: PV type x under/between panels x grazing/mowing; three permanent 3x3 m releves per treatment, repeated over nine dates (216 records).
Production outcome: Actual grazing established but animal growth, meat/wool yield, stocking rate, feed intake and welfare were not measured. Vegetation biomass INDEX (coverage percent x maximum height), not harvested biomass mass. Table 1 total index: mowing 58.40, grazing 23.98; reported SD 19.13 and 8.35. Eighty-three plant species recorded.
Energy / LER outcome: Site description reports rotating-section annual production 650 MWh, almost the same as stationary section. No observation year or meter-series method given; do not label as study-measured generation or assign exact stationary output.
Microclimate / water / welfare: Water use and animal drinking supply NR. Microclimate effects mainly discussed from literature, not quantified as site treatment outcomes. | No measured animal welfare endpoints; discussion about cable chewing is not a quantified site incident rate.
Missing data / source issues: Sheep breed/count/stocking density, grazing calendar, animal production and welfare, PV module manufacturer/model/count/power, tilt and row spacing NR.
Study limitations: Vegetation proxy study, not animal productivity or experimental fire trial. Table labels index as %/m, whereas equation multiplies percent by height in m; units unresolved. Prose approximately 30% lower index under grazing does not agree with 23.98 versus 58.40 (about 59% lower by arithmetic); preserve Table 1 and flag conflict. No observed reduction in fire frequency demonstrated. Site total capacity derived, component areas unknown.
Source pages: All 9 PDF pages reviewed; pp.2-3 site/equipment/grazing; p.4 Table 1 and index definition visually verified; pp.5-7 vegetation interpretation; pp.8-9 conclusions/references.

Site / country: Cascadilla Community Solar Array, adjacent to Cornell University, Ithaca, NY, USA
Species / cultivar: Finnsheep, Dorset, East Friesian sheep and crosses; 136 sheep
Area definition: Whole solar site reported as 54 acres; converted using 4046.8564224 m2/acre. Five fenced areas total 48.4 acres; not interchangeable with whole-site area.
Comparator: Mowed controls, five grazing densities, shade versus open inter-row areas, seeded versus unseeded plots
Implementation evidence: 136 sheep grazed an operating, named ground-mounted solar array over three seasons (PDF pp. 1-2).
Production outcome: Forage production decreased with grazing density; shaded areas produced up to 2.5 times less forage. No lamb weight gain, meat or milk yield reported.
Microclimate / water / welfare: Body condition declined with increasing density (P<0.001); FAMACHA density effect P=0.059, no significant pairwise differences. Densities 12-16 sheep/acre suggested as a compromise for flock condition.
Missing data / source issues: PV capacity, modules, tilt, installation year, electricity, actual grazing fees and costs not reported. DOI and publication year not identifiable in supplied document. Exact forage yields and BCS are graphical; not digitized.
Study limitations: Preliminary results. Avoid equating instantaneous grazing density with annual stocking rate. Nutrition subset n=10 is preliminary. No full economic budget.
Source pages: PDF pp.1-3 site and design; pp.3-6 results; p.1 secondary grazing-fee claim

Site / country: Animal Biometeorology Laboratory, Sao Paulo State University, Jaboticabal, Brazil
Species / cultivar: Seven crossbred Holstein x Gyr heifers (7/8 Holstein); mean 242 kg, SD53.5; age 10 months
Study period: Authors report 18 consecutive observation days, 2-20 April 2019; electricity September 2018-August 2019; six heifers in subsequent 12-day methane assessment
Capacity status / basis: Calculated 10 x 335 Wp /1000; Fronius inverter separately reported 3 kWp
Area definition: PV roof 4 x 5 m; paddock 1900 m2; projected shade 19.3 m2, 2.76 m2/heifer
Comparator: Voluntary time in sun versus PV shade, not randomized separate herds
Implementation evidence: Seven heifers studied under ten operating modules with monitored annual electricity (PDF pp.3,5,7).
Production outcome: No milk yield, weight gain or reproduction effect quantified; heifers were not lactating.
Energy / LER outcome: 4869.4 kWh monitored September 2018-August 2019; distinct period from A0059 calendar 2019.
Microclimate / water / welfare: Reported radiant heat-load reduction 40%; body surface and skin temperatures reduced by 6 and 4 C with shade under increasing irradiance; respiratory rate lower in shade above 600 W/m2 (P<0.05).
Missing data / source issues: Installation date, azimuth, OPEX, replacement costs, explicit tariff and price/currency conversion date NR. Reported 18 days and date range 2-20 April retained without reconciliation. Figure extraction includes embedded duplicate draft text; duplicates not separate evidence.
Study limitations: Small observational shade-use study; methane evaluated separately after field measurements. Electricity displacement offsets are calculated, not a reduction in animal emissions. Payback omits a detailed cash-flow budget.
Source pages: PDF p.3 animals and system; p.5 energy/methane methods; pp.7-10 results and economics

Site / country: Rabbit Hills Solar Farm, Oregon State University, Corvallis, Oregon, USA
Species / cultivar: Weaned Polypay lambs; grass-dominated pasture overseeded with festulolium, white clover, chicory and plantain
Study period: 17 April-12 June 2019 and 30 March-11 June 2020; forage monitoring extends beyond spring grazing
Orientation / tracking: Rows oriented east-west; panels tilted south
Area definition: Whole solar farm 2.4 ha; experimental area separately 0.6 ha
Spacing definition: Reported rows 6 m apart; authors describe 3 m fully shaded and 3 m partially shaded areas
Comparator: Adjacent open pasture grazed by lambs
Implementation evidence: Two-year lamb grazing experiment inside an operating 1.4 MW solar farm (PDF pp.2-3).
Production outcome: 2019 ADG solar/open 120/119 g/head/day (P=0.90); 2020 89/92 (P=0.64). Reported liveweight production 2019 1.5/1.3 and 2020 4.6/5.0 kg/ha/day, no significant treatment difference. Values retained as reported; 2019 per-area figures do not readily reconcile with described stocking rates.
Energy / LER outcome: Forage LER 1.81 (2019), 1.68 (2020); lamb LER 2.04 and 1.97. Electricity ratio assumed equal to 1, not measured.
Microclimate / water / welfare: Open pasture used 0.72 L/head/day more water in late spring 2019 (P<0.01); 2020 open/solar 1.48/1.32 L/head/day, not significant (P=0.42).
Missing data / source issues: Installation year, module count/model and measured electricity not reported; no CAPEX/OPEX, discount rate or full cash-flow model. Text p.5 ordering of fully/partially shaded forage yields conflicts with Fig.2 and narrative; do not assign these totals to treatments without qualification.
Study limitations: Three replicates; spring lamb production only. Growth differences not statistically significant. LER includes assumed electricity ratio. Author-labelled return is not a complete farm profitability calculation.
Source pages: PDF p.2 site/design; p.3 management/economic method; pp.5-8 results; p.10 economic limitations
